text.p: Bonds eased as a weaker U.S. market dragged Europe down. But local bonds held up better than Germany and Spain, so spreads at the longer end narrowed, traders said.
The market was illiquid and is likely to remain so on Friday because of the holiday in Spain, they added.
The trend on Friday will be set by the direction of the Bund, they said.
"The market closed down after the New York opening, with profit-taking eating away all the morning's gains," said one trader.
The lack of liquidity was particularly acute at the short end, helping drag the spread between the two and the 10 year bonds down to a mere 97 basis points.
